source_text: Ut autem quae sunt acta, breviter repetamus, arbitrium liberum, quod in mali parte vitiorum voluptatibus vel diaboli persuasionibus, in boni autem parte virtutum dogmatibus et variis gratiae divinae speciebus iuvatur, non potest aliter constare, nisi ut et iustitiae ab eo et peccati necessitas auferatur.
pass_a_gloss: But that we may briefly repeat what have been transacted: free choice, which on the part of evil is helped by the pleasures of vices or the persuasions of the devil, but on the part of good by the dogmas of virtues and various species of divine grace, cannot otherwise stand, unless both the necessity of justice and of sin be taken away from it.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: To repeat our conclusions briefly: free will is assisted on evil’s side by the pleasures of vice or the devil’s persuasions, and on good’s side by teachings of virtue and the various forms of divine grace. It cannot exist unless necessity is removed from it in respect of both justice and sin.

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
